goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same mistake: the end time is computed from slotStartTime when it should use slotEndTime.

goldens.comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
goldens.reasoning: C2 flags the same problem: comparing dayjs objects with === checks references, not values, so the comparison is always false.

candidates: Working-hours validation computes both start and end from slotStartTime instead of using slotEndTime for end, allowing slots that extend past workingHour.endTime

Dayjs equality comparison uses === which is reference equality and will always be false, making the intended special-case branch unreachable for date overrides where start and end represent the same instant

Multiple date override ranges on the same day are treated as intersection (slot must be inside all ranges) rather than union (slot valid if inside any range) due to find() logic rejecting slots outside any single override range
Date override offset calculation uses Date.toString() and re-parses it via Dayjs which is redundant and may cause subtle parse/precision issues across runtimes
